question: The game's place list comes from the 2025 Census Gazetteer, which covers the 50 states, D.C. and Puerto Rico only, so none of the four other inhabited territories has a single place a life can start in. For Guam, the U.S. Virgin Islands, American Samoa and the Northern Mariana Islands, give the official list of places a resident would say they live in, with their Census 2020 Island Areas codes: (1) each territory's county-equivalent units (Guam; St. Croix, St. John, St. Thomas; American Samoa's Eastern, Western and Manu'a districts and Swains Island; the Northern Islands, Rota, Saipan and Tinian municipalities) with their five-digit FIPS codes; (2) the places or census designated places inside each, with their seven-digit place codes and 2020 populations; (3) the spelling a resident uses, including the okina and glottal marks where official names carry them (for example Hagåtña, Nu'uuli), and the plain spelling a search box should also accept; (4) which of these is a unit of local government in its own right (Guam's 19 villages with elected mayors; the Northern Mariana Islands' four municipalities with elected mayors and municipal councils; American Samoa's villages under matai and county councils; the U.S. Virgin Islands, which has no municipal government) versus a statistical place only. Say the source and vintage for each list.

title: Which towns and villages a life can start in on Guam, the U.S. Virgin Islands, American Samoa and the Northern Mariana Islands
usableAnswer: One table per territory: place name as a resident writes it, a plain-letter search spelling, the Census 2020 Island Areas place code, the county-equivalent it sits in, its 2020 population, and whether it is a local government with elected officers (and which), with the source and vintage of each column.
whyItMatters: lamontae asked on September 23, 2026 for a life in every territory. To let one start today, the territories thread seated a marked placeholder list of well-known villages and towns (src/simulation/territory-places.ts on branch claude/project-thread-ysy15i), keyed in its own namespace rather than with invented Census codes. Every such key is a provisional identity: once real place codes arrive the list is replaced and a crosswalk carries existing saves forward. Until then the placeholder list may omit villages and the population of each is unknown, so nothing in the game may treat a territory town's size as known.
